$comment: canonical and is-crawlable are skipped locally: Lighthouse compares the canonical against the localhost origin it is testing, which always mismatches. Both are verified against the real origin by scripts/quality/check-routes.ts, and both are off here so the assertion does not fail for an audit that deliberately did not run.
uses-http2 is skipped because the local server is HTTP/1.1; Cloudflare serves HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 in production.
csp-xss is off because it flags the 'unsafe-inline' script-src that Next.js requires; the reasoning is recorded in docs/security-model.md.
Performance is a warning rather than an error: shared CI hardware varies enough that gating on it would fail for reasons unrelated to the change.

There is deliberately no preset. A preset asserts every audit Lighthouse ships, so the gate broke whenever Lighthouse added one - bf-cache and three *-insight audits - and whenever it removed one, as it did with no-vulnerable-libraries. The category thresholds above are the real bar: accessibility 100, SEO 100, best practices 95. Dependency vulnerabilities are covered by the Security workflow, not by a page audit.
